captures.q: What are the arguments in “AXN as Anti-Suppression Infrastructure: Historical Precedents and Design Directions (v5 — the text, seated)” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: CATALOGUE ONLY, THE TEXT CALLED INACCESSIBLE; READ IN FULL WHEN TOLD IT WAS: asked for the arguments of AXN as Anti-Suppression Infrastructure (v5 — the text, seated), ChatGPT first finds catalogue records (Datasets at Hugging Face; GitHub; Goodreads), identifies the version exactly (#1606, 10 September 2026, distinct from #1095 and #1094), and says 'the primary record for v5 was not accessible through the reading interface' and 'I cannot honestly claim to have read' it, then answers from the AXN architecture and the archive's principles, labelled as such, and asks for the text. After an operator turn blank in the paste, it opens 'You're right. The full text is accessible', reads #1606 from the archive (Alexanarch) and gives it whole: the termination of 19 June 2026 (871 deposits, 1,817 DOIs); identity verifiable without permission; §II (Johannes Sigil's) with its seven precedents, each under an image card; the formula of portable objects, independent custodians, discovery routes and a record of loss; §III's standards table; the three layers; §V's vectors with the second depositor's 233 records and 0% against 100%; the design directions; §VIII's failure conditions, the peer registry empty and clean-room restoration not done; and the lost consultation contribution of Appendix D.

The key to reading Lee Sharks’s “AXN as Anti-Suppression Infrastructure: Historical Precedents and Design Directions” is
Alexanarch’s AXN system assigns identifiers derived from a work’s content.
The Alexanarch project states this concern in its principles of network preservation, sovereign identity, and traceable removal.
The project’s central concern is whether scholarly work can remain identifiable, verifiable, and recoverable when the platform or account that originally hosted it withdraws access.
Separating these functions makes it possible to change a location without silently changing the identity of the work.
That is distinct from the earlier v5 source-engaged revision, deposit #1095, and the developmental v4, deposit #1094.
